title: Research
text:
This page is adapted from my research statement at ccgoller.com/research.


Bacterial pathogens that cause disease in healthcare settings and vulnerable populations threaten patient care and have spread rapidly across the globe. My research focuses on understanding microbial trends and characteristics associated with persistence and treatment evasion. By combining broad molecular epidemiological surveys with targeted screens for novel inhibitors, I aim to identify directed therapies that reduce the spread of emerging pathogens.
These projects are intentionally designed to be accessible and training-rich. Many approaches are relatively inexpensive, straightforward, and safe for undergraduate participation while still producing meaningful data on microbial mechanisms and behavior.




Microbial pathogenesis and antimicrobial strategy development.
Molecular epidemiology of clinically relevant microorganisms.
Undergraduate-centered discovery projects in microbiology and genomics.
Environmental and applied microbiology, including waste reduction and recycling opportunities.




I am committed to bridging clinical and basic science through collaborations with clinical microbiology laboratories, clinicians, ecologists, bioinformaticians, and basic scientists. The goal is a research ecosystem that is both a vibrant training environment and a productive program for discovery.




Full research statement page: https://ccgoller.com/research/
Research projects index: https://ccgoller.com/research-projects/

title: Teaching
text:
This page is adapted from ccgoller.com/teaching-philosophy and ccgoller.com/courses.


The mysteries of nature inspire innovation and scientific discovery, but scientific literacy is essential for everyone in an interconnected world. I am committed to making science more accessible by engaging students as participants and co-creators in the learning process.
My teaching framework emphasizes discovery, collaboration, and communication: discover, teach, and share together.

Teaching philosophy page: https://ccgoller.com/teaching-philosophy/
Teaching philosophy PDF: https://carloscgollerphd.blog/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/teaching-philosophy-v2-4.pdf

title: Carlos C. Goller
text: Carlos C. Goller is a Teaching Professor at North Carolina State University in Raleigh, NC. He teaches microbiology, life science, public health, and other fun courses as part of the Department of Biological Sciences. When not playing with Delftia acidovorans or code, Carlos enjoys spending time with his family and playing with his dog Sunshine.
